  your PR. Furthermore, for new integrations, it gives an impression of how
  the configuration would look like.

```yaml

sensor:
  - platform: bbox
    host: 192.168.1.1
    monitored_variables:
      - down_max_bandwidth
      - up_max_bandwidth
      - current_down_bandwidth
      - current_up_bandwidth
```

Closing this PR as it violates the above mentioned architecture decisions. 

I am sorry @schmurtzm this integration will need to be changed by implementing a config flow.

See [ADR-0010](https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/blob/master/adr/0010-integration-configuration.md) for more details:

> These rules apply to all new integrations. Existing integrations that should not have a YAML configuration, are allowed and encouraged to implement a configuration flow and remove YAML support. Changes to existing YAML configuration for these same existing integrations, will no longer be accepted.

issue_context.title: No option to set IP for Bbox Router bandwidth as sensors
issue_context.body:

  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
By default it take ip 192.168.1.254 but many bbox users change that. It should be possible to specify an IP in configuration.yaml

@HydrelioxGitHub may be you can help ;)

[bbox documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/bbox)
[bbox source](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/bbox)

## Environment

HA supervised inside proxmox on intel nuc

    Home Assistant Core release with the issue:
    0.114.3
    Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known):
    0.112 i do not recall it being this bad
    Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core):
    supervised inside proxmox


- Integration causing this issue: bbox
- Link to integration documentation on our website: 
https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/bbox

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
- platform: bbox
#  host: 192.168.0.1      <----- This option does not exist for [sensor.bbox]
  monitored_variables:
    - down_max_bandwidth
    - up_max_bandwidth
    - current_down_bandwidth
    - current_up_bandwidth
    - uptime
    - number_of_reboots
```

## Traceback/Error logs

  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

## Additional information
comments:
It should be possible in theory

The python library that is beneath how this integration works (Pybbox) can handle to specify a custom ip when you start to communicate with a bbox. 

Unfortunately I've change my FAI so I does not own a Bbox device any more so I can't really test new dev.

It seems already implemented in  "[device_tracker.py](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/bbox/device_tracker.py)".

@HydrelioxGitHub , may be I can do some tests with your help ?
Yes it seems it does. And on line 202 of the sensor.py file, the Bbox object is initiated without any ip in parameters so it takes 192.168.1.254 by default.

Hey guys, I have looked over this issue and decided to implement the missing option.
Unfortunately, I do not own a bbox router myself, so could you please test this addtion @schmurtzm?
Thanks a lot ✌

Thank you @springstan it seems perfect ! 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7110113/91470837-80fc2200-e895-11ea-94fe-bc59967df1fa.png)

review_comments:
This violates both ADR-0007 & ADR-0010.

I do not think we should make an exception to these rules.
Completely agree after reading them. My initial thought process was just to "fix" this missing option but I understand that this would lead to even more exceptions which we should not encourage.
